exposure: Women cared for in private antenatal services
Women cared for in public antenatal services
Model of antenatal care (public vs. private)
cohort: 5957 women residing in the Reggio Emilia Province, Italy, who delivered between October 2010 and November 2011
finding: The public model of antenatal care, involving both midwives and obstetricians, was associated with lower rates of cesarean section and ultrasound scan utilization compared to the private model, led by obstetricians only, without a significant difference in negative perinatal outcomes.
mod_finding: Women receiving care in a private obstetrics model had a slightly higher probability of cesarean section compared to those in a public model involving both midwives and obstetricians.
